# Context Mode **A free, local plugin for 10 coding agents. It keeps tool output out of your agent's context window and keeps all usage data on your machine. The plugin is free forever.** [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/context-mode?label=npm%20downloads)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/context-mode) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/mksglu/context-mode?style=flat&color=yellow)](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1478479412700909750?label=Discord&logo=discord&color=5865f2)](https://discord.gg/DCN9jUgN5v) [![License: ELv2](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-ELv2-blue.svg)](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/blob/v2.1.10/LICENSE) **33K GitHub stars · 683K npm downloads** (read 2026-11-01, [stats.json](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/blob/v2.1.10/stats.json)) · on the Hacker News front page and GitHub Trending: [charts and sources](#adoption-stars-and-npm-downloads) > The Context Mode plugin is free and local, with its source open on GitHub. **Context Mode Gateway** is a separate hosted service with its own account and subscription. It takes the same idea from tool output to the whole conversation: Gateway Recall keeps long sessions searchable, and Gateway Memory shares what your agents learn across sessions and tools. [See how the Gateway works](https://contextmode.ai/docs/how-saving-works?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=quote) **Contents:** [Why](#why) · [Adoption](#adoption-stars-and-npm-downloads) · [Install](#install) · [Try it](#try-it) · [Use cases](#use-cases) · [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Tools](#tools) · [Security and privacy](#security-and-privacy) · [Context Mode Gateway](#context-mode-gateway) · [License](#license) · [Community](#community) ## Why A coding agent reads files, runs commands and fetches pages, and every result goes into its context window. The Context Mode plugin runs that work in a local sandbox, keeps the full output in a SQLite index on your machine, and gives the agent the part it asks for. - **The plugin is free forever.** Use it at home and at work, free of charge, under a source-available license. - **Runs on your machine.** The hooks, the sandbox and search run as local processes next to your agent. - **The plugin keeps your data on your machine.** Every index lives in `~/.context-mode`: one `context.db` per project. - **Zero telemetry.** The plugin keeps all usage data on your machine. [Security and privacy](#security-and-privacy) lists each network call it makes. - **Works offline after install.** Sandbox runs, file indexing and search use local SQLite and your own runtimes. - **Thinking in Code.** The agent writes a short script instead of reading the data, and only what the script prints reaches the context: see [How it works, step 5](#thinking-in-code). - **Small replies.** On the 36 bench rows with 10 KB or more of raw output, the plugin's median reply is 99.4% smaller than the raw output. ## Adoption: stars and npm downloads
Open the [interactive chart](https://contextmode.ai/open-source/stats?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=adoption#daily) and point at a bar to read its value. Tabs there show days, weeks, months and years. Stars come from the GitHub GraphQL API (`starredAt`); npm downloads come from `api.npmjs.org/downloads/range`. The total up to 2026-10-29 is 683K npm downloads (`stats.json` keeps a daily copy). A daily job redraws both charts. - **Hacker News.** "MCP server that reduces Claude Code context consumption by 98%" reached the front page with 570+ points and 107 comments on 2026-02-28 ([thread](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47193064)). - **GitHub Trending.** A bot that watches GitHub Trending logged the repo there on 14 days from 2026-04-24 to 2026-10-17 ([uibm/trending-watcher](https://github.com/uibm/trending-watcher/issues?q=%22mksglu%2Fcontext-mode%22)). Starred by engineers at these companies: each name is the company field of 2 or more stargazer profiles, read with the GitHub GraphQL API on 2026-11-01 ([data](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/blob/v2.1.10/docs/assets/readme/data/stargazer-companies.json)). ## Install Pick your agent: [Claude Code](#install-claude-code) · [Codex](#install-codex) · [Gemini CLI](#install-gemini) · [Qwen Code](#install-qwen) · [Pi](#install-pi) · [OpenCode](#install-opencode) · [Copilot CLI](#install-copilot-cli) · [Kiro](#install-kiro) · [VS Code](#install-vscode) · [ZCode](#install-zcode) Open its block and copy its own install command. Each block also holds the update, check and remove steps, and the [Install guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/install?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=install) walks through them. The plugin needs Node 24.15.0 or later, from the engines field in [package.json](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/blob/v2.1.10/package.json). On Windows, add Git for Windows: the shell tools run in Git Bash, and doctor checks for it. contextmode installs as the npm package and command `context-mode`. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Qwen Code install from GitHub, and each of their commands names the release branch.
Claude Code ```sh claude plugin marketplace add mksglu/context-mode claude plugin install context-mode@context-mode ``` ```sh # update claude plugin update context-mode@context-mode # check claude plugin list # remove claude plugin marketplace remove context-mode ``` Hooks ✓ (package) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓

VS Code (Copilot) ```sh npm i -g context-mode context-mode setup --agents vscode ``` ```sh # update context-mode upgrade # check context-mode doctor --agents vscode # remove context-mode setup --remove --agents vscode ``` Hooks ✓ (hook file) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓
ZCode ```sh zcode plugins marketplace add mksglu/context-mode zcode plugins install context-mode@context-mode ``` ```sh # update zcode plugins update context-mode@context-mode # check zcode plugins list # remove zcode plugins uninstall context-mode@context-mode ``` Hooks ✓ (hook file) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓
The npm route works for every agent: ```sh npm i -g context-mode context-mode setup ``` Setup is also the repair. It shows a plan, saves your earlier config, then applies the plan; when a step ends early, it restores the saved config. To uninstall: ```sh context-mode setup --remove npm rm -g context-mode ``` Restart the agent, then run `/ctx-doctor` in it. Each check prints PASS or a fix command, and the [Doctor guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/doctor?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=install-doctor) explains each check.
How we tested the install Every agent gets hooks, the MCP server and the plugin skills; the last line of each block above says how. Hooks reach each agent in one of three ways: in the plugin package (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code), in a hook file (Codex, Copilot CLI, Kiro, VS Code, ZCode), or in a plugin inside the agent (OpenCode, Pi). The [Agents guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/agents?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=install-agents) shows what each agent runs. We ran the real binary of each agent with the plugin hook: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Pi, OpenCode, Copilot CLI and ZCode. Each run used a clean temp home and a local test model, on 2.0.0-next.15. For VS Code and Kiro, the check covers the hook setup: VS Code runs the hook command with the documented payload, and kiro-cli 2.35.2 loads all 6 hook entries. CI runs setup, doctor, a hook and an MCP handshake for all 10 agents from the packed package on Linux, macOS and Windows. Record: [HOOKS-FIRE.md](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/blob/v2.1.10/docs/architecture/release/HOOKS-FIRE.md). Each agent uses its own install command, and [ADR-0023](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/blob/v2.1.10/docs/architecture/adr/ADR-0023-native-install.md) says why.
Your first task with the plugin, step by step: [First session](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/first-session?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=install-next). Or paste a prompt from [Try it](#try-it) right now. ## Try it Paste one of these prompts into your agent after the install. Each one ran once, live, in Claude Code 2.1.312, and its answer matched the source data ([evidence and rerun steps](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/blob/v2.1.10/bench/evidence/try-it-2026-11-02/README.md)). The headline numbers in [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) use the median of 5 runs. Other agents do the same job with the same tools: `ctx_execute`, `ctx_index` and `ctx_search`. After a prompt, run the stats skill and read the report yourself ([See the saving](#see-the-saving)). ```text On https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffect, show me the example that connects to a chat server and cleans up, and list the rules for the dependency array. ``` The hook sends WebFetch to the sandbox, and the agent searches the page for the example and the rules. 601,984 B raw, 20,860 B reached the context, 96.5% saved (2026-11-02, 2.0.0-next.26, claude-haiku-5-5). ```text Fetch https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/photos. Which photo has the longest title (give its id and title), and how many photos have a title that contains the word "est"? ``` The agent runs code over 5,000 JSON records in the sandbox and gets back two answers. 1,039,898 B raw, 393 B reached the context, 99.96% saved (2026-11-02, 2.0.0-next.26, claude-haiku-5-5). The answer is two short facts, so this is the best case of the four. ```text Here is a Linux syslog sample: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/logpai/loghub/master/Linux/Linux_2k.log. How many authentication failures does it contain, and which 3 remote hosts caused the most? ``` The agent counts failures in a 1,999-line syslog in the sandbox. 216,485 B raw, 566 B reached the context, 99.7% saved (2026-11-02, 2.0.0-next.26, claude-haiku-5-5). ```text What are the top 10 stories on the Hacker News front page right now? Give title, points and domain for each. ``` The hook sends WebFetch to the sandbox, and the agent reads ten stories from the page. 35,087 B raw, 1,501 B reached the context, 95.7% saved (2026-11-02, 2.0.0-next.26, claude-haiku-5-5). The front page changes, so the raw size changes with each run. ### See the saving Run the stats skill right after a prompt. Each agent uses its own command; the skill calls `ctx_stats` and shows its report unchanged. | Agent | Command | |---|---| | Claude Code | `/ctx-stats` | | Codex | `$ctx-stats` | | Copilot CLI | `/ctx-stats` | | Gemini CLI | `Call ctx_stats and show me the report.` | | Kiro | `Call ctx_stats and show me the report.` | | OpenCode | `Call ctx_stats and show me the report.` | | Pi | `/skill:ctx-stats` | | Qwen Code | `Call ctx_stats and show me the report.` | | VS Code (Copilot) | `/ctx-stats` | | ZCode | `Call ctx_stats and show me the report.` | The first lines of a real report, after the JSON prompt above ran as one `ctx_execute` call: ```text context-mode stats ────────────────────────────────────────────────────� …[文件过长——仅保留首 16KB 与末 8KB]… ebp" alt="Gateway Spend: spend per day by model, cost per request and cache hit rate">
Spend. Spend per day and per model, cost per request and the cache hit rate, to help you plan a budget.

Three prompts to try with the Gateway on. The line under each one names the feature it shows. ```text Move this project from Jest to Vitest. Convert every test file, fix the config, run the suite after each batch, and tell me what is left. ``` Memory keeps the plan and the file list across a long job. ```text Pick up where we stopped yesterday on the Jest to Vitest move. What is done, what is left, and which test was failing? ``` Recall brings back yesterday's work in a fresh session. ```text Which date library did we choose on Tuesday, and why did we reject the other two? ``` Search finds the answer in past sessions.
Gateway features, from contextmode.ai/docs Source: [contextmode.ai/docs](https://contextmode.ai/docs/how-saving-works?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=features): | Feature | What it does | What you get | Details | |---|---|---|---| | Context Saving | Folds old tool output, runs data work as code (Thinking in Code), trims tool schemas, places cache marks | A tool output over 2,048 B becomes a short pointer, with the full copy archived | Saves the most on sessions with many tool calls | | Recall | The model sees recent work and an index of older work; the agent searches the archive for the rest | Gateway, Claude Code, Opus 5.5, 200K window, 2026-10-04: mean cost per session $4.8627 to $3.0353 (-37.6% in dollars, `ab.json` below) | Cost measured in Claude Code on Claude Opus 5.5 | | Memory | Each fact keeps two times: when it was true and when the Gateway learned it | Claude Code and Codex on one account share one store, tested end to end | The memory block goes into the first request of a new session | | Skills | A skill catalog on the Gateway for your account; it loads the skill that matches your message | The matching skill loads on the message that needs it | Import skills from GitHub; a loaded skill joins the prompt in full | | Search | Searches the prompts, commands and tool output that passed through, in the console and as an agent tool | Find any past prompt, command or tool output, from the console or your agent | The console searches the first 4,000 characters of each tool result | | Session resume | One command rebuilds a conversation as a native Claude Code or Codex session | Continue a conversation in Claude Code or Codex | Restores the text, tool names and a summary; the command is valid for 15 minutes | | Active Context | Sets how much a thread carries before its oldest parts move to the archive: 200K, 500K or 1M tokens | Pick the window size per thread | An image older than the kept part becomes a short text note | | Instructions | One text of at most 4,096 characters that tells every agent how to answer you | Read from the provider cache after the first request | Sets how the agent writes to you | | Protect | A tool-call firewall: checks shell commands, file reads and writes, web fetches and tool-server calls by what they do | Each call checked before it runs | Reads the call itself, so keep your agent's sandbox on for script files and paths built at run time; opt-in | | Prompt caching | Keeps requests cache-friendly: cache marks on the fixed part of the prompt and a cache for fetched pages | Inside the measured costs above | Uses up to 4 cache marks, the provider's maximum | | Live and Analytics | Shows each request and what the Gateway saved, as it happens and over time | See each request and its saving, live and over time | Covers every request that passes through the Gateway |
Gateway only: its cost against Claude Code alone, Claude Opus 5.5, mean dollars per session at list price. The plugin numbers are in [Benchmarks](#benchmarks). - Six short tasks (2026-09-29): 24.5% fewer dollars pooled over 176 sessions (21% to 29% per task). [v3-opus55-short.json](https://contextmode.ai/benchmarks/data/v3-opus55-short.json?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=bench) - Long Claude Code session, 200K window (2026-10-03/04): mean cost per session $4.8627 to $3.0353 (-37.6% in dollars, mean of 3 pairs). [ab.json](https://contextmode.ai/benchmarks/recall/200k-r2/ab.json?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=bench) - We fixed the rules before each run: [contextmode.ai/docs/benchmarks](https://contextmode.ai/docs/benchmarks?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=bench). The Gateway routes to Anthropic and OpenAI. The Gateway sends your requests to its server on the way to the model. It keeps a searchable record of your sessions for Recall and Search, and masks secrets and e-mail addresses when it reads archived output back. Its privacy page is at [contextmode.ai/privacy](https://contextmode.ai/privacy?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=privacy). Keep your agent's own sandbox on next to Protect. ## License Elastic License 2.0 (ELv2, the `LICENSE` file), a source-available license.
